renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Some people live in lower doctrines — Vaiṣṇava ones all the way down to southern tantras — or took vows there. A few even stand high but serve unqualified gurus. When the Lord turns them around with his power falling on them, here's the drill.

First they fast. Next day, after they've worshipped with the plain everyday mantras and told everything they did, you walk them in front of God. Then they pick up their old vow and throw it in the water. Then they bathe. Then you sprinkle them, clean them up with sacred rice and a tooth-stick, walk them in blindfolded, and do the full worship for God with the plain mantras.

Then the fire itself gets turned into Śiva with those same plain mantras, and you clean their vow in it. You pack their name inside their own mantra and say I clean whats wrong ending with svāhā — a hundred times. Then one more full ladle into the fire, ending with vauṣaṭ.

Then you call the old Vow-Lord, worship him, and tell him straight from Śiva: you do this guy no harm. You announce that, you feed him, you send him off — and you send the fire off too. That's called lifting the liṅga. After that it's the usual settling-in and the rest, same as before.

And from then on, you start people whenever you want. But everywhere here, in the śrāddha rite, image-abandonment is chief — so says the revered Siddha view; and its rule will be told in the occasional-rites teaching.

paragraphs.text: Lower doctrines, all the way down — Vaiṣṇava to southern tantra — plus vow-takers, plus high-seaters serving unqualified gurus. Lord drops power, turns them around: here's the drill.
Fast first. Next day: plain-mantra worship, tell-all, walk-in before God. Grab the old vow, drown it. Bathe. Sprinkle, rice-and-stick clean, blindfold walk-in, full God-worship with plain mantras.
Fire goes Śiva-fied by the same plain mantras — clean the vow in it. Name packed in own mantra, I clean whats wrong, svāhā, times a hundred. Then one more full ladle, vauṣaṭ out.

Call the old Vow-Lord, worship him, read him his orders straight from Śiva: zero harm to this guy. Announce, feed, dismiss him — dismiss the fire too. That's liṅga-lifting. Settle-in and the rest as usual.
From now on: start people whenever. But everywhere here, in the śrāddha game, image-dropping is chief — Siddha-view says so; its rule drops in the occasionals teaching.
